recipes.name: Jicama Appetizer
ingredients_raw: 1 jicama, peeled and cut into bite-sized pieces

steps.text: Arrange jicama on a platter. Sprinkle lime juice and chili powder over the jicama. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Jicama Appetizer
raw_recipe.description: All you need for this refreshing treat is raw jicama, lime, and chili powder. This is a quick and easy recipe with a delicious crunch.
raw_recipe.name: Jicama Appetizer
recipeIngredient: 1 jicama, peeled and cut into bite-sized pieces

review.reviewBody: As others have mentioned, this is a common way to serve jicama in Mexico. If you have a Mexican section in your supermarket, try to find a seasoning in a shaker bottle called "tajin" that combines lime, salt and chiles. It is used for everything here, and is what I use to sprinkle on jicama. Love it.

I liked it, and my husband did also, but we both thought that 2 tablespoons chili pepper was way too much. It was thick and pasty on the jicama, and I ended up rubbing my pieces off on a paper towel to remove some of the powder. Next time I will just sprinkle a light coating on and add to taste.

My jicama was on the small side, so I only used one tablepoon of chili powder. Also, before I juiced the limes, I zested them and threw the zest in as well. I thought this tasted a little flat, so I added a sprinkling of garlic powder, some kosher salt and a good grinding of pepper. I probably ended up using more than 2 tablespoons of lime juice, I just squeezed two limes over the jicama. I was quite pleased with the end result and I'm taking these to work to snack on. Thanks so much for the post, BECCAS911!

All new to me and wonderful. Loved it plain. Loved it this way. And also made jicama hash with diced jicama, onions, peppers, and a smidge of garlic sauteed in a couple of tablespoons of olive oil, salt, chili powder....good with eggs. I am delighted to discover a new (to me) taste and texture

I remember my mother making a jicama fruit salad. She would put oranges, jicama, cucumbers and mango, lime juice, salt and Chile powder. Sometimes it was just the jicama, like this recipe. Delicious either way. I use Tajin (a combo of spices, Chile and lime juice) and fresh squeezed lime juice. I love it!

This is delicious, nutritious (very high in Vit. C), very low calorie, and so easy! Love the crunch. I've used just cayenne pepper before but chili powder is much better. To get the jicama completely covered with lime juice I put it in a container with a sealable top, add the juice, cover and shake. I didn't measure but did use more than 2 T lime juice. Then I put it on a serving plate and sprinkle with the chili powder. Any leftovers stay fresh in the fridge for quick snacks, and to add smaller pieces to a salad for a nice crunch.
As posted, it is bland. I doctored it and it turned out very tasty: Blend cilantro, 1/2 de-veined and seeded jalepeno, honey, rice vinegar and fresh squeezed lime.
Fabuloso! I used to eat this all the time when I was a student in Mexico. You can use lemon juice if you don't have fresh lime juice, although lime is better to me.

This didn't do it for us, so we poured rice wine vinegar over it and added salt, and that was better. I think there's not enough lime juice called for here, probably because the size of "1 jicama" can vary a lot; you may need to adjust on the fly. For our tastes this required the addition of salt. (Note: I added a cucumber and doubled the recipe, but left the chili powder measurement the same, due to the color.)

The lime was a really great addition to the jicama which can be rather bland when it comes to taste. 

This almost didn't make the cut when I was deciding which appetizers to serve, but was surprised by how many people enjoy jicama!

Cool, crisp, low-cal munchy on a hot summer day.
This was simple and a little nicer than just being plain. I’ll make it again.

Tasty, very easy, crunchy and refreshing. My Mex-Flavors-loving hubby really likes it as an accompaniment to our noontime meal. I seem to rarely use a whole jicama when I’m making other recipes and now I have a simple way to add spice to a meal AND use up the rest of the jicama!
My preferred seasoning of choice is Tajin. This needed more lime juice.

This is a very common way to serve jicama cold in many of the southeast Asian countries such as Thailand, Singapore, Malaysia, Philippines and the Hawaiian Islands besides in some central and South American countries. The crunchy sweet mixed with the fresh lime juice and a kick of the chili s so refreshing. Easy to make and a big hit with a crowd.
I used Tajin instead of chili powder and have made it several times. Loveit! Eating some now with a sandwich instead of chips. Yummers!
My mom use to make this when I was a kid. It's very easy to make.
